decisions.reason: As a core-related pipeline component for the firm’s established infrastructure customers, the dismantling joint is still more likely to be retained, although its disappearance from later website evidence raises some rationalization risk.
The pipe support bracket fits the firm’s fabrication capabilities and project customer base well, so it is likely to stay, with only a limited risk from portfolio streamlining.

The powder-coated public waste bin is a relatively distant, single-product diversification from the core pipeline business and is therefore the most likely to be discontinued if resources are refocused.
The waste-bin-with-ashtray line is outside the core offer but still uses the firm’s metalworking and coating strengths and can address municipal buyers, so it has a fair chance of being kept.

Outdoor public ashtrays are a niche and non-core product line, and despite some overlap with municipal customers they are more likely than not to be cut in favor of core business or newer developments.
